correctness.rationale: Riemann–Roch gives the exact integral formula \(\chi((r,D,u),(s,E,v))=rv+su-rs\chi(\mathcal O_X)+s(D\cdot K_X)-D\cdot E\). Point and line-bundle classes surject onto \(\mathbf Z\oplus N^1(X)\oplus\mathbf Z\), and nondegeneracy of the intersection form identifies the kernel with the numerical radical. In the resulting basis the Euler matrix is explicitly reduced by integral unimodular operations to \(H\oplus(-Q)\). This proves the Smith factors and cokernel statement. Hodge index fixes the determinant sign and yields the positive value \(|\det Q|\). The packaged exact verifier replays the matrix operations, determinant identity, and Smith-factor equality on independent integral test matrices.

value.rationale: The initiating paper explicitly asks what geometry forces numerical Cartan determinant one. In dimension two the theorem gives a complete unconditional answer: the determinant is exactly the absolute Néron–Severi discriminant, so determinant one is equivalent to intersection-lattice unimodularity. The stronger Smith statement determines the full finite defect group, not merely one scalar, and translates categorical Euler-lattice arithmetic into a classical surface invariant. This also sharpens the obstruction supplied by non-unimodularity to maximal numerical exceptional structures.
